items.q: What is staffing?
also: what does a staffing company do
items.a: Staffing is the process of finding, screening, hiring and placing the right people in the right jobs. A staffing company works for client companies: it understands their hiring needs, sources candidates, screens and interviews them, and places the selected people as permanent employees, contract staff or temporary workers.

items.q: What are the types of staffing?
also: kitne tarah ki staffing hoti hai
items.a:
Main types of staffing:
1. Permanent staffing: the candidate joins the client's payroll directly; we charge a one-time placement fee.
2. Contract / temporary staffing: the candidate works at the client but stays on our (or a third-party) payroll for a fixed period; we bill monthly.
3. Contract-to-hire: starts as contract, client can convert to permanent later.
4. Executive search: senior and leadership hiring with a dedicated search process.
5. RPO (Recruitment Process Outsourcing): we run part or all of the client's hiring.
6. Project / bulk hiring: large numbers of similar roles in a short time.

items.q: What is our recruitment process?
items.a:
Standard end-to-end recruitment process:
1. Requirement intake: get the job description (JD), budget, location, experience, notice period and number of openings from the client.
2. Sourcing: job portals (Naukri, LinkedIn, Indeed), our database, referrals, social media.
3. Screening: check CV against JD, then a phone screening call (skills, CTC, notice, location).
4. Submission: share shortlisted profiles with the client in the standard format.
5. Interviews: schedule and coordinate client interview rounds, collect feedback.
6. Offer: negotiate CTC, release offer, get acceptance.
7. Pre-joining follow-up: stay in touch during notice period to avoid drop-outs.
8. Joining and onboarding: confirm joining, documents, and raise the invoice.

items.q: What details should we take from the client for a new requirement?
also: client se requirement me kya poochna hai
items.a: Requirement intake checklist: job title, number of positions, detailed JD, must-have and good-to-have skills, experience range, salary / CTC budget, location and work mode (office / hybrid / remote), shift timings, notice period accepted, education requirements, interview rounds and panel availability, target closing date, replacement / guarantee terms, and the client's point of contact.

items.q: Where do we source candidates from?
items.a: Main sourcing channels: Naukri.com, LinkedIn (Recruiter and posts), Indeed, Foundit (Monster), Shine, Apna and WorkIndia (for blue-collar and entry level), our internal candidate database, employee and candidate referrals, WhatsApp and Telegram job groups, Facebook groups, campus drives, and job fairs. For niche or senior roles, LinkedIn headhunting and referrals work best.

items.q: How do I do a Boolean search for candidates?
items.a:
Boolean search combines keywords with operators:
• AND: both terms must appear: Java AND Spring
• OR: either term: (Developer OR Engineer)
• NOT / minus: exclude: Java NOT JavaScript
• Quotes: exact phrase: "business analyst"
• Brackets group terms.
Example: ("Java Developer" OR "Backend Engineer") AND (Spring OR "Spring Boot") AND Microservices NOT Intern. On Naukri, also use the experience, location, notice period and salary filters.

items.q: What questions should be asked in a screening call?
also: screening call me kya poochna hai
candidate ko call pe kya puche
items.a:
Screening call checklist:
1. Current company, role and total / relevant experience.
2. Key skills and recent projects matching the JD.
3. Current CTC, expected CTC and whether negotiable.
4. Notice period, and whether buy-out or early joining is possible.
5. Current location and willingness to relocate / work mode preference.
6. Reason for job change.
7. Other offers or interviews in progress.
8. Availability for interviews.
9. Communication skills (judge during the call).
Always tell the candidate about the role and company briefly and confirm interest before submitting.

items.q: How to shortlist CVs?
items.a: To shortlist CVs: match must-have skills first, then experience range, location and notice period. Check job stability (frequent switches under 1 year are a red flag), relevance of recent projects, education requirements and salary fit. Look for gaps and ask about them. Keep 3 to 5 strong profiles per opening rather than sending many weak ones; quality submissions improve the client's interview-to-offer ratio.

items.q: What is the format for submitting profiles to clients?
items.a: Submit each profile with a short summary on top: Candidate name, Current role and company, Total experience, Relevant experience, Key skills, Current CTC, Expected CTC, Notice period, Current location, Preferred location, Reason for change, and Recruiter remarks (why this candidate fits). Attach the updated CV. Send profiles in one email per requirement with a clear subject like: Profiles for <Job title> - <Client> - <Date>.

items.q: How do we schedule interviews?
also: interview ka time kaise fix kare
items.a: Interview scheduling: take 2 to 3 time slots from the client panel, confirm one with the candidate, then send a calendar invite / email to both with date, time, mode (video link or office address), interviewer name, round and documents to carry. Send a reminder to the candidate a day before and 1 to 2 hours before. After the interview, collect feedback from both sides within 24 hours and update the tracker.

items.q: What to do if a candidate does not show up for the interview?
items.a: If a candidate is a no-show: call and message immediately to find out the reason, inform the client honestly and offer a reschedule only if the reason is genuine. Mark it in the tracker. To reduce no-shows: confirm the day before, confirm again on the morning of the interview, share the exact location / link, and keep a backup candidate ready.

items.q: How to reduce offer dropouts?
items.a:
To reduce offer dropouts:
• Check the real reason for job change and counter-offer risk during screening.
• Ask about other offers honestly before submission.
• Keep the offer competitive and close the offer quickly.
• Stay in touch weekly during the notice period (calls, WhatsApp, client connects).
• Share company updates, team intro, joining kit details.
• Watch for warning signs: delayed responses, resignation not submitted, asking for joining date extensions.
• Always keep a backup candidate for critical roles.

items.q: How to handle a counter offer from the current employer?
also: candidate ko current company retain kar rahi hai
items.a: Handle counter offers early: during screening ask "If your company offers a hike, will you stay?" Remind the candidate of their real reasons for leaving (growth, role, culture), since money rarely fixes those. Most people who accept counter offers leave within a year. If the candidate still wavers, inform the client early and activate the backup candidate.

items.q: What is notice period and buyout?
items.a: Notice period is the time an employee must serve after resigning (usually 30, 60 or 90 days in India). Buyout means the employee or the new employer pays the old employer for the unserved notice days so the candidate can join early. Many companies also allow early release if handover is completed. Always confirm the notice period and buyout option in screening.

items.q: What is CTC, gross and in-hand salary?
also: ctc aur take home me fark
items.a: CTC (Cost to Company) is the total yearly cost of an employee to the company: basic + allowances + employer PF + gratuity + bonus / variable + insurance etc. Gross salary is CTC minus employer contributions like employer PF and gratuity. In-hand (take-home) salary is gross minus deductions like employee PF, professional tax and income tax (TDS). Roughly, monthly in-hand is about 75 to 85 percent of monthly CTC for most salaries.

items.q: How to negotiate salary with a candidate?
also: candidate zyada salary maang raha hai
items.a: Salary negotiation tips: know the client's budget and market range before talking; ask for current and expected CTC with breakup; understand what matters to the candidate besides money (role, growth, location, work mode); explain the full value of the offer (variable, benefits, learning). A typical hike on switch is 20 to 40 percent; above that, justify with skills. Never promise a number before the client approves.

items.q: What is the placement fee for permanent hiring?
items.a: Permanent placement fees in India are usually a percentage of the candidate's annual CTC: about 8.33 percent (one month) for junior and bulk roles, 10 to 15 percent for mid-level roles, and 15 to 25 percent for senior / niche / leadership roles. The fee is billed after the candidate joins, with payment terms usually 30 to 45 days. Check the signed agreement with each client for exact terms.

items.q: What is the replacement guarantee?
also: candidate chhod gaya to kya hoga
items.a: A replacement guarantee means if a placed candidate leaves or is terminated within a fixed period after joining (commonly 60 to 90 days), we provide a replacement candidate free of cost, or refund / credit the fee as per the agreement. It does not apply if the role, salary or terms are changed by the client, or if the client terminates the role itself. Exact terms are in each client agreement.

items.q: How does contract staffing billing work?
also: contract staffing ka billing kaise hota hai
items.a: In contract staffing the employee is on our payroll and works at the client. Each month we bill the client: employee's monthly CTC (salary + PF + ESI + other statutory costs) plus our service charge (markup), commonly 5 to 15 percent of CTC or a fixed amount per head, plus GST at 18 percent. Attendance is confirmed with the client before invoicing.

items.q: What statutory compliances apply to contract staff?
items.a: Key compliances for contract staff in India: PF (12 percent employee + 12 percent employer on basic, for basic up to the wage ceiling or as opted), ESI (0.75 percent employee + 3.25 percent employer for gross up to ₹21,000 per month), Professional Tax (state-wise), Labour Welfare Fund (state-wise), minimum wages, payment of bonus, gratuity (after 5 years), Contract Labour (CLRA) registration and licences where applicable, and timely salary payment with payslips. Confirm current rates with your payroll / compliance team since they change.

items.q: What is background verification?
items.a: Background verification (BGV) checks that a candidate's details are true: identity (Aadhaar / PAN), address, education certificates, previous employment (dates, designation, exit reason via HR), reference checks, criminal / court record check, and sometimes credit or drug tests. It is usually done after the offer and before or just after joining, by the client or a BGV vendor, with the candidate's written consent.

items.q: What documents are needed at joining?
also: joining ke liye kya documents chahiye
items.a: Common joining documents: offer letter acceptance, updated CV, Aadhaar and PAN, passport size photos, educational certificates and marksheets, previous company offer letter, relieving letter / resignation acceptance, last 3 months' payslips, bank account details (cancelled cheque), UAN / PF number, address proof, and Form 16 or previous employer income details for tax.

items.q: What is the onboarding process?
items.a: Onboarding steps: send a welcome email with joining date, time, address and documents list; collect and verify documents; complete HR forms (PF, ESI, bank, nomination); issue ID card, laptop and system access; induction about company, policies and team; assign a buddy / manager; set 30-60-90 day goals. In staffing, also confirm joining to the client and raise the invoice.

items.q: What metrics do we track in recruitment?
items.a: Key recruitment metrics: time to fill (requirement open to offer accept), time to hire, submissions per requirement, submission-to-interview ratio, interview-to-offer ratio, offer acceptance rate, offer-to-join ratio, early attrition (within 90 days), cost per hire, source of hire, and revenue per recruiter. Healthy targets: submission-to-interview 40 percent+, offer-to-join 80 percent+.

items.q: What is the daily target for a recruiter?
items.a: A typical recruiter daily target: 60 to 100 candidate calls (connect rate around 30 to 40 percent), 15 to 25 good screenings, 3 to 6 quality submissions, and interview follow-ups for every active candidate. Monthly targets are usually set in joinings or revenue, for example 3 to 6 joinings per month for IT mid-level roles. Your team lead may set specific targets.

items.q: What is an ATS?
items.a: An ATS (Applicant Tracking System) is software to manage hiring: store candidate profiles, track each requirement and candidate status (sourced, screened, submitted, interview, offer, joined), schedule interviews, send emails and generate reports. Examples: Zoho Recruit, Ceipal, Recruit CRM, Freshteam, Greenhouse, Lever. All candidate data and status changes should be updated in the ATS daily.

items.q: What are the candidate status stages?
items.a: Standard candidate stages: Sourced → Contacted → Screened → Submitted to client → Shortlisted by client → Interview scheduled → Interview round 1 / 2 / final → Selected → Offer released → Offer accepted → Joined. Negative stages: Not interested, Rejected (screen / client / interview), Offer declined, Dropped / No-show, Backed out.

items.q: How to write a good job description?
items.a: A good job description has: clear job title; 2 to 3 line company and role summary; key responsibilities (5 to 8 bullets); must-have skills and experience; good-to-have skills; qualification; location, work mode and shift; salary range (improves response a lot); benefits; and how to apply. Use simple words, avoid internal jargon, and keep it under 400 words.

items.q: How to post a job on Naukri and LinkedIn?
items.a: Job posting tips: use the exact job title candidates search for, add the key skills as tags, set location, experience and salary range, write a clear JD, and add screening questions (notice period, CTC, location). On LinkedIn also share the post from recruiter profiles with hashtags (#hiring #jobs #<skill>) and ask the team to engage. Refresh / repost every 7 to 10 days to stay on top.

items.q: How to do bulk hiring?
also: ek saath bahut log hire karna
items.a: Bulk hiring approach: freeze a clear JD and simple selection criteria; post on Naukri, Apna, WorkIndia, Indeed and WhatsApp groups; run walk-in drives and campus drives; use a short screening script and pre-recorded assessments; batch the interviews on fixed days; make same-day offers where possible; and track daily funnel numbers (sourced, screened, interviewed, selected, joined). Plan for 20 to 30 percent dropouts.

items.q: How to plan campus hiring?
items.a: Campus hiring steps: shortlist colleges by course and past results, contact the placement officer, fix the date, share the JD and eligibility (branch, percentage, backlogs), run a pre-placement talk, online test, group discussion / technical round and HR round, announce results the same day if possible, release offer letters, and stay in touch till joining since freshers have high dropout rates.

items.q: How does the employee referral program work?
items.a: Employee referral program: employees refer candidates for open roles; if the referred person is hired and completes the required period (commonly 90 days), the referrer gets a referral bonus as per company policy. Referrals usually join faster and stay longer. Submit referrals through HR or the ATS with the candidate's CV and consent.

items.q: How to collect interview feedback?
items.a: Collect feedback from the client within 24 hours of each interview: selected / rejected / on hold, strengths, gaps, and next round details. Share honest feedback with the candidate the same day. Record it in the ATS. If the client is slow, send a polite reminder after 24 hours and call after 48 hours; delayed feedback is a top reason candidates lose interest.

items.q: How do we onboard a new staffing client?
items.a: New client onboarding: understand their hiring plan and pain points; share our company profile; agree commercials (fee percentage, payment terms, replacement period); sign the agreement / MSA and NDA; get vendor registration done (GST, PAN, bank details, MSME if applicable); set up a single point of contact on both sides; agree the submission format and feedback turnaround; then start with the first requirements.

items.q: When do we raise the invoice for a placement?
items.a: For permanent placements, raise the invoice on the candidate's joining date (after the client confirms joining), as per the fee in the agreement plus 18 percent GST. Mention candidate name, position, joining date, CTC and fee percentage. Follow up for payment as per the payment terms (usually 30 to 45 days). For contract staffing, invoice monthly after attendance confirmation.

items.q: How to hire blue-collar workers?
items.a: Blue-collar hiring (delivery, warehouse, factory, security, drivers, helpers): use Apna, WorkIndia, Naukri (Jobhai), local agencies, WhatsApp groups, pamphlets and walk-ins near the location. Keep the process short: one screening call, document check and a simple trial or interview. Clearly explain salary, shift, PF / ESI, incentives and stay or food facilities. Same-day or next-day joining works best.

items.q: How to hire for IT roles?
items.a: IT hiring tips: understand the tech stack (languages, frameworks, cloud, databases), use Boolean search on Naukri and LinkedIn, check GitHub or portfolio for developers, ask about real project work and their own contribution, take a short technical screening question if possible, and check notice period early since 60 to 90 days is common. Hot skills (cloud, data, AI, full stack) need faster processes and competitive offers.

items.q: How should we maintain the candidate database?
items.a: Keep every candidate in the ATS / database with: name, phone, email, skills, experience, current and expected CTC, notice period, location, last contacted date, status and remarks. Update after every call. Tag candidates by skill and domain so they can be reused for future requirements. Follow data privacy: use candidate data only for hiring, with their consent, and never share it outside without permission.

items.q: How to inform a candidate about rejection?
items.a: Inform rejections quickly and politely, by call or message: "Hi <Name>, thank you for your time with <Client>. They have decided to move ahead with other profiles for this role. Your profile is strong in <skill>, and I will reach out for matching roles soon." Share useful feedback if the client gave any. Good rejection handling keeps candidates willing to work with us again.

items.q: What is an exit interview?
also: employee chhod raha hai to kya poochna
items.a: An exit interview is a conversation with an employee who is leaving, to learn why they are leaving and what could improve: reasons for leaving, what they liked, issues with role, manager, pay or culture, and suggestions. Findings help reduce attrition. In contract staffing, also confirm handover, asset return, and final settlement (F&F) timelines.
